technical_findings.description: The migration forbids automatic rollback to a JSON-only binary, but the preserved release workflow captures the previously released backend image and automatically redeploys it after deployment or smoke failure. The plan does not specify how the first Identity migration establishes a compatible captured rollback target or prevents the existing automatic rollback from selecting the JSON-only predecessor. Merely documenting a compatible image does not change that workflow. Once source credentials are removed, this rollback cannot preserve account/session authority.

specs/022-modern-auth/plan.md:72 states the compatible-binary requirement; Verification and release preserves the existing release workflow.

technical_findings.recommendation: Specify an executable, gate-preserving transition sequence that establishes and verifies the compatible rollback target before import commitment. Choose an explicit compatibility rollout or an audited migration-aware rollback selection/guard, identify the affected implementation paths, and rehearse failure after import commit, source cleanup, and resumed auth writes through the actual release rollback mechanism.

technical_findings.description: The external-Google-email flow has no fully specified transition from mailbox verification to signed-in completion. Provider completion returns verify_mailbox, while email verification declares provider_mailbox_verified and permits session creation only for signed_in. The only provider completion request requires the original one-use handoff code, whose lifetime is at most 60 seconds, whereas mailbox verification may take up to ten minutes. The contracts do not identify a finalizing response or a replacement continuation authority, so clients cannot implement this journey consistently after the original handoff expires or is consumed.
evidence: specs/022-modern-auth/plan.md:94 requires mailbox proof before durable creation for new Google third-party addresses.
specs/022-modern-auth/contracts/http-auth.md:33 lists provider_mailbox_verified and states that only signed_in may create a session.
specs/022-modern-auth/contracts/http-auth.md:42 requires handoff_code for provider completion; line 48 makes it one-use and at most 60 seconds.
specs/022-modern-auth/contracts/http-auth.md:56 lists verify_mailbox as a provider completion outcome.
specs/022-modern-auth/data-model.md:10-12 defines mailbox-required attempts, 60-second handoffs, and ten-minute challenges without an explicit continuation transition.
technical_findings.recommendation: Define the exact mailbox-required completion edge and matching web/native response contract. For example, consume the callback handoff when entering the client-bound mailbox-required state, then let successful mailbox verification atomically finalize that same staged provider attempt and return signed_in. Alternatively, specify a bounded replacement continuation proof and its endpoint. Preserve the original callback evidence, client binding, attempt lifetime, uniqueness checks, and one-use semantics.

Include this evidence in the eventual acceptance task.

technical_findings.description: The new HTTP contract requires owner/session/client checks but does not specify 404 for a resource belonging to another caller. It declares owner_mismatch and includes 403 among new failures, while omitting 404 entirely. This leaves the distinction between failed same-account reauthentication and wrong-owner resource access undefined.
evidence: docs/decisions/0001-vnext-modular-monolith-and-workflow-contracts.md: Authorization and privacy assumptions requires owner-scoped reads, transitions, references and lists, with 404 for a wrong owner.
.specify/review-rubrics/security-privacy-reviewer.md: Ownership and authorization explicitly classifies unstated wrong-owner 404 semantics as at least important.
specs/022-modern-auth/contracts/http-auth.md: Common rules defines owner_mismatch without a status mapping; Email and recovery, Providers and Additive account management declare failures without 404.
technical_findings.recommendation: Add an explicit contract rule and endpoint status declarations for owner-restricted lookups: foreign resources and nonexistent resources return indistinguishable 404 responses before disclosure or mutation. Preserve 403 for failed reauthentication of the caller's own account. Specify any expected-owner mismatch rejected before lookup separately, and require negative evidence that foreign account, attempt and challenge references neither disclose existence nor mutate authority.

technical_findings.description: Interrupted verification, password reset and account changes are described with 'Nothing was changed' even when the request may have committed before its response was lost. Atomic server writes do not make the outcome observable to the client. The design also directs users to retry without distinguishing an unsubmitted action from a consumed one-use proof.
evidence: specs/022-modern-auth/design.md:62 — D-02/M-02 lost-network state says 'Nothing was changed. Reconnect, then try again.'
specs/022-modern-auth/design.md:76 — D-03/M-03 explicitly says not to assume reset success but supplies 'Nothing was changed' copy.
specs/022-modern-auth/design.md:89 — D-04/M-04 connection-loss state also says 'Nothing was changed'.
specs/022-modern-auth/contracts/http-auth.md:24 — reset changes the password and revokes sessions atomically.
specs/022-modern-auth/contracts/native-auth.md:19 — a lost completion response requires a fresh attempt rather than replaying the consumed proof.
technical_findings.recommendation: Add stable completion-unknown states for D/M-02, D/M-03 and D/M-04. Use copy such as 'We couldn't confirm whether this finished. Your local tasks are kept.' Specify the next safe action for each flow: check current account state or sign in again through the same account, and obtain fresh proof when necessary. Reserve 'Nothing was changed' for confirmed rejection or cancellation before mutation.

technical_findings.description: The Apple unlink/deletion flow has a planned local-success/remote-cleanup-failure outcome, but the design supplies no stable state or user-facing copy for it. D-04/M-04 partial failure only covers loading method metadata, and its generic update error claims existing methods were retained, which would be false after successful local unlink.

specs/022-modern-auth/design.md:87 — generic account error says 'Your existing sign-in methods are kept.'

technical_findings.recommendation: Define stable unlink/deletion result variants for remote revocation pending and unconfirmed. State that BrainBuddy access removal or deletion scheduling succeeded, that Apple cleanup is being retried or could not be confirmed, and that the purge deadline remains unchanged. Specify where this disclosure appears if the action ends the caller's session.

technical_findings.description: The proposed empty password_hash representation introduces a timing oracle through the preserved public password-login endpoint unless its verification path changes explicitly. Current verification rejects an empty hash immediately as InvalidHashError, whereas an unknown account performs an expensive Argon2 dummy verification. An attacker could distinguish passwordless registered addresses from unknown addresses despite identical error responses. The plan specifies the new representation but does not specify the compensating verification behavior or its regression evidence.
evidence: specs/022-modern-auth/plan.md, Phase 1 A: password_hash remains a mandatory string, with "" representing an unset password; the known dummy timing hash must never be assigned.
specs/022-modern-auth/data-model.md, users row and Authority invariants: passwordless accounts use an empty password hash.

backend/app/services/auth_service.py, AuthService._verify_password: InvalidHashError returns False immediately; AuthService.login performs dummy Argon2 verification only when the user lookup returns None.
docs/auth.md, decision 5: password login must not disclose account existence through response wording or verification timing.
specs/022-modern-auth/quickstart.md, Browser journeys: the planned negative evidence does not cover passwordless-versus-unknown password verification cost.
technical_findings.recommendation: Amend the technical plan and validation matrix so unset or invalid password hashes perform comparable dummy Argon2 verification work and then reject unconditionally. Keep the dummy hash outside account persistence and never treat matching its known password as successful authentication. Add a focused deterministic regression check proving unknown and passwordless accounts both invoke the expensive verification path and that every passwordless password attempt fails without issuing a session.
